<thought>From the spectrum, the M+1 peak (~13 % of the base) matches the expected 13 C contribution of roughly a dozen carbons, indicating carbon. The prominent M+2 peak (~33 % of the base) aligns with the characteristic 35Cl/37Cl isotopic ratio (~3:1), allowing definitive identification of chlorine. No other element shows a distinctive isotopic pattern (e.g., bromine’s ~1:1 M+2, sulfur’s ~4 % M+2). Therefore the elements that can be definitively identified are carbon and chlorine.</thought>
<final_answer>['C', 'Cl']</final_answer>
